note: Explicit service id -> OpenRouter model id map. fetch_specs.py never guesses: a service without an entry here gets no specs block. match values: 'named' = the catalog card or the OpenRouter description names this exact model; 'vendor_family' = the row is the vendor's flagship family for that product, the product's own served model is not published; 'none' = no defensible mapping, no specs shown.

chatgpt.why: OpenRouter describes this id as the alias that 'always resolves to the latest Instant chat model used in ChatGPT'.

claude.why: Anthropic's assistant runs on the Sonnet tier; the alias follows the latest Sonnet so the weekly refresh stays current. Anthropic does not publish which model each plan serves.

gemini.why: Gemini app spans Pro and Flash tiers; the Pro alias is the paid tier. Free tier serves Flash, so the numbers here are the Pro row.

deepseek.why: DeepSeek's flagship reasoning model. The card describes the family, not a single version.

qwen.why: OpenRouter calls Qwen4 Max 'the flagship model in Alibaba's Qwen4 series'.

kimi.why: The card names Kimi-K2. Note the discrepancy: this row lists 131k context while the card claims a 1M window, so the block shows 131k and the claim stays visible in the text.

zhipu-glm.why: OpenRouter describes the alias as 'the latest GLM model from Z.ai'.

gigachat.why: Sberbank's own model, not served through OpenRouter. No row to read.

alisa.why: Yandex's assistant and YandexGPT models are not served through OpenRouter.

perplexity.why: Sonar is Perplexity's own search model family; the product runs on it.

grok.why: OpenRouter describes the alias as 'the latest Grok model from xAI'.

veda-ai.why: Belarusian aggregator of other vendors' models; it has no model of its own to measure.

dedii.why: Aggregator that routes to Claude, Gemini and Perplexity; no single model of its own.

librachat.why: No published model identity; nothing to map without guessing.

mistral-vibe.why: Le Chat runs on Mistral's Large tier; the card describes the product, not a pinned version.

hunyuan.why: The card names the family as 'Hunyuan (Hy4)'; OpenRouter lists this id as 'Tencent: Hy4'.

stepfun.why: The card names Step 5; OpenRouter lists this id as StepFun's flagship for agentic work.

mimo.why: The card names MiMo-V2-Flash; OpenRouter's current Flash row is V2.6, so the version differs from the card.

ernie.why: The card names the ERNIE-5.5 release. OpenRouter only lists the free preview row for it, and that row prices at $0, so the block shows the preview's own price, not Baidu's paid API.

llama.why: Meta's open-weight flagship on OpenRouter; the card describes the Llama family.

nemotron.why: NVIDIA's open frontier-reasoning flagship in the Nemotron 3 line.

reflection-ai.why: OpenRouter describes Beam 1.0 as Reflection's open-weight reasoning model; the card does not name a version.

inkling.why: The card names Inkling and OpenRouter lists the same id.

microsoft-copilot.why: A product bundling several vendors' models; no single row describes it.

meta-ai.why: The card says Meta AI runs Llama, so the same row is shown here as on the Llama card.

character-ai.why: Character.AI serves its own models; they are not listed on OpenRouter.

you-com.why: A multi-model product; no single row describes it.
